lt: 2006 m. atlikti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, Panerių g. 8. Darbai vykdyti Šv. Stepono bažnyčios buvusios klebonijos kieme. Iš viso tyrinėtas 37,5 m2 plotas. Iki pradedant archeologinius tyrinėjimus, nedalyvaujant archeologui iškastas 12 m2 plotas sklypo R ir apie 15 m2 plotas V dalyse. V dalyje buvo aptikta žmonių kaulų [p. 253].
en: In 2006 archaeological excavations were conducted in Vilnius at Panerių St. 8. The work was performed in the courtyard of the former rectory of St. Stephen’s Church. A total area of 37.5 m2 was investigated. Four graves with human remains were found. It is conjectured that they found the territory of former cemeteries, a large part of which were destroyed in the early 20th century. The burials date to no earlier than the 18th century.

lt: Žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai rekonstruojant dujotiekio tinklus Kauno senamiestyje buvo atliekami 2006 m. birželio– rugpjūčio mėnesiais. Buvo numatyta atviru būdu atkasti dujotiekio tinklus šurfais sujungimuose, posūkiuose ir ventiliacijos šulinių vietose, į senus vamzdžius įstumiant naujus plastmasinius. Dujotiekio tinklai Kauno senamiestyje buvo nutiesti XX a. 7–8 dešimtmetyje, kai archeologiniai tyrinėjimai statybos metu dar nebuvo atliekami [p. 289].
en: In 2006 the gas main pipes were reconstructed in the E part of Kaunas Old Town. This was a continuation of work performed in 2002. During the reconstruction the old pipes were excavated using test pits at turns, branches, and home connections. 162 test pits of various sizes were excavated and a field survey conducted in an area of 591.4 m2. 218.4 m of undisturbed cultural layer cross-sections were recorded. The layers have survived only fragmentally in one slope of the ditch or in part of it. Only sterile soil was found in many test pits. Of the 162 test pits excavated, cultural layer cross-sections were recorded in 84 (almost 50 %). The cultural layers in the test pits excavated in streets were characteristic to streets. Present-day Nemuno St. formed at the site of an old road to Vilnius. Layers that were from 0.7–1 m to 1.5–1.9 m thick and characteristic to gardens and farmland were found in the majority of the test pits deeper in the quarter. The earliest development in this part of the Old Town is known from the late 18th – early 19th century. Only a few 16th–17th century archaeological finds: household pottery sherds characteristic to Kaunas Old Town, were collected in conduct

In 2006 excavations and field evaluations were conducted at various locations in Vilnius. A floor dating to the 16th – 1st half of the 17th century and the 18th century was found at Didžioji St. 25–4. Late 16th–17th century finds as well as 16th and 18th century coins were also discovered there. The remains of late 19th – early 20th century buildings and finds dating to the 16th–19th centuries were found at Pylimo St. 17. 16th–17th century and 18th–19th century finds were discovered in a mixed earth layer at Totorių St. 16 / 16–1. The remains of a mid-18th century brick building, a fragment of an earlier (17th century) pavement, and the remains of wooden well were discovered at Totorių St. 20. 17th–19th century finds and five late 18th century coins stuck together in a solid mass were also found. The foundation of a building dating to the 17th century as well as 16th–19th century finds were discovered at Trakų St. 14.

t: Tyrinėjimai Rotušės aikštėje ir jos prieigose
lt: 2006 m. LII MTS ekspedicija tęsė archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniaus senojo miesto vietoje, Rotušės aikštėje ir jos prieigose (žr. ATL 2005 metais, V., 2006, p. 363). Darbai susiję su Rotušės aikštės rekonstrukcija. Pirmiausia tirta Dižþiosios g. atkarpa tarp Dižþiosios g. 19 (kavinė „Amatininkų užeiga“) ir Etmonų g. Antruoju etapu tirta aikštės Š dalis tarp Stiklių–Savičiaus–Didžiosios g. sankirtos ir Didžiosios g. 12 (Šv. Nikolajaus cerkvė). Trečiuoju etapu pratęsti ūkinės duobės, atrastos 2005 m., tyrinėjimai [p. 365].
en: In 2006 the excavation in Vilnius Town Hall Square and its approaches were continued. A 19th century stone pavement was recorded between Didžioji St. 19 and the Contemporary Art Centre. A disturbed cultural layer with individual 16th–19th century finds was recorded under it. A disturbed cultural layer 0.5 m thick was recorded at greater depths at the trench sites. Several iron couplings from wooden water pipes, seals, coins, and stove tile fragments were found in it. The fragments of kiosk foundations and two (17th and 15th–16th century) pavement levels were discovered between Stiklių and Savičiaus Sts. and St. Nicholas Orthodox Church. A zoomorphic pendant and a halfgroat (½ grossus) of Alexander Jagiellon were found there. Fragments of the foundation of a 15th century merchants’ building with a basement and stairwell were found in line with Stiklių – Savičiaus Sts. The excavation of a storage pit from the 2nd half of the 16th century also continued. The layer in it was 2 m thick. Bones, leather fragments, pottery sherds, seals, and coins were found in the pit.

lt: 2006 m. LII MTS vykdė archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniaus senojo miesto vietoje, Subačiaus g. 11. Tyrinėjimai vykdyti būsimo piligrimų viešbučio statybos vietoje. Anksčiau čia vykdytų archeologinių tyrinėjimų metu aptikti XIX a. pastatų pamatai, XIV–XV a. puodžiaus dirbtuvių ūkinė duobė su gausiais tam laikotarpiui būdingais buitinės bei statybinės keramikos fragmentais (žr. LIIR, f. 1, b. 1441; ATL 1994 ir 1995 metais, V., 1996, p. 247–249; ATL 1996 ir 1997 metais, V., 1998, p. 403; ATL 2005 metais, V., 2006, p. 362) [p. 368].
en: In 2006 an excavation was conducted at Subačiaus St. 11 in Vilnius Old Town. An area of about 140 m2 was excavated. Two oven hearths, artisans’ (a jeweller’s, a bone craftsman’s, and a potters’) storage pits with production waste, three (19th, 17th and 16th century) pavement levels, and the stone foundations of two wooden buildings were found. A cultural layer of up to 3 m that dates to the late 14th – 19th century was recorded. In all over 7000 finds were discovered during the excavation: household and construction pottery sherds, stove tile sherds, metal and glass artefacts, fragments of leather footwear, and coins.

lt: 2006 m. LII MTS vykdė archeologinius žvalgymus Vilniuje, Vilniaus ir Klaipėdos g. sankirtoje, Moniuškos skvere, kur pagal suderintą projektą buvo atliekami jo tvarkymo darbai [p. 372].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in Moniuškos Sq. at the intersection of Vilniaus and Klaipėdos Sts. in Vilnius. Fill layers dating to the late 19th–20th century and fragments of late 18th–19th century brick walls were recorded in it. Between the Benedictine monastery and the fence enclosing Moniuškos Sq. on the E an 18th century brick installation for storing quick and hydrated lime was discovered at a depth of 0.8 m. Fragments of 18th–19th century brick buildings were discovered at a depth of 0.6–1.7 m near the brick wall enclosing the Square on the E. The subsoil was not reached in the greater part of the lot. The lower layers were not excavated.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai Paupio g. 28 ir Polocko g. 21A
lt: 2006 m. rudenį LII MTS atliko žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniuje, Paupio g. 28, UAB „Vilniaus kailiai“ fabriko ir Polocko g. 21A, buvusio UAB „Vilijos siuvimo fabrikas“ teritorijose [p. 374].
en: In 2006 the LII MTS conducted an evaluation in Vilnius at Paupio St. 28. 9 test pits with a total area of 27.25 m2 were excavated. During the evaluation a cultural layer of up to 3.1 m thick and dating to the 16th–20th centuries was recorded. Household and structural ceramic sherds as well as leather fragments were discovered in it. It was established that the top horizons of the cultural layer in the excavated territory were formed in the 20th century. The bottom horizons of the cultural layer go back to the 16th century but no clear data about the development of the land in this period was obtained. An evaluation was also conducted in Vilnius Old Town at Polocko St. 21A. 9 test pits with a total area of 22.75 m2 were excavated. During the evaluation a cultural layer, which was up to 3.15 m thick and dated to the 17th–20th century, was recorded. Household and structural ceramic sherds were discovered. An 18th century enclosing wall made of stones bonded with lime mortar was recorded. A stone pavement dating to the 17th–18th century was found.

lt: 2006 m. Barboros Radvilaitės g. 6 pastato aplinkoje, pamatų sanavimo tranšėjos vietoje vykdyti archeologiniai žvalgymai (žvalgytas 113 m2 plotas). Jų metu nejudintas kultūrinio sluoksnio horizontas nepasiektas, archeologinių radinių neaptikta. Barboros Radvilaitės g. 4, 6 sklype atliekant archeologinius tyrinėjimus iškasti 6 archeologiniai šurfai (ištirtas 48,5 m2 plotas) [p. 377-378].
en: In 2006 an excavation was conducted in Vilnius at Barboros Radvilaitės St. 4, 6. An area of 117 m2 was excavated. The cultural layer reaches a depth of over 2.2–2.5 m, the top layers having been destroyed to a depth of up to 1.2–1.4 m in the 20th century. 16th–19th century archaeological finds, fragments of 18th–19th century stone pavements, and the remains of 19th – early 20th century brick walls were found.

t: Tyrinėjimai Maironio g. 11 ir Šiltadaržio g. 6
en: In 2006 an excavation were conducted in Vilnius at Maironio St. 11 in the former Bernardine monastery complex. Fragments of 16th, 17th, and 20th century brick walls were found at the sites of trenches for rehabilitating the foundations of the S and E buildings while 16th–19th century finds were discovered in the mixed cultural layer. 16th–19th century finds were discovered inside the S and E buildings. During an excavation in 2006, a cultural layer of up to 2.1 m thick, which was destroyed in the 20th century, was discovered inside the building at Šiltadaržio St. 6 in Vilnius. An arched 17th century foundation was unearthed.

lt: 2006 m. atliekant vandentiekio magistralės Nr. 36 renovacijos darbus apie 140 m2 plote atlikti archeologiniai žvalgymai. Didžiausios apimties žemės kasimo darbai vykdyti Pylimo g., keli šurfai iškasti Geležinkelio g. Archeologiniai žvalgymai suteikė naujų duomenų apie kultūrinio sluoksnio pobūdį, išlikimo laipsnį įvairiose vietose šioje (V ir PV) Vilniaus senojo miesto dalyje [p. 379].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in an area of about 140 m2 on Pylimo and Geležinkelio Sts. During them a 15th–20th century cultural layer was recorded. Brick constructions, conjectured to be the remains of bridges, were discovered opposite the locations of the Trakai and Rūdninkai Gates in the city’s defensive wall. The remains of brick sewers and wooden water pipes as well as wooden construction elements – the remains of bastion fortifications (?) from the 19th – 1st half of the 20th century were also found. 16th–20th century archaeological finds were discovered at the evaluated sites.

lt: Vilniuje, sklype Sodų g. 14, buvusio „Gintaro“ viešbučio aplinkoje yra numatyta vykdyti užstatymo darbus. Prieš juos teritorijoje 2006 m. atlikti archeologiniai žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai, kuriais siekta nustatyti esamos teritorijos kultūrinio sluoksnio bei galimų užstatymų chronologiją [p. 342].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in Vilnius at Sodų St. 14 on a lot that is slated for development. During it, 38 survey test pits with a total area of 164 m2 were excavated. 17th – 20th century cultural layers were recorded. The earliest wooden building at this location dates to the 17th century, the earliest brick one to the late 18th – early 19th century.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai pastatų komplekse T. Kosciuškos g. 3
lt: 2006 m. atlikti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniaus piliakalnio su papiliais (A 1961K) teritorijoje, pastatų komplekse T. Kosciuškos g. 3, pastatuose 02 (šurfai 1–4) ir 06 (šurfas 5). Ištirtas 20,4 m² dydžio plotas [p. 385].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in buildings 02 (test pits 1–4) and 06 (test pit 5) of the building complex at T. Kosciuškos St. 3 in Vilnius. An area 20.4 m² in size was excavated. The largest part of the cultural layer consisted of a fill layer up to 2.4 m thick from the second half of the 19th century that contained finds dating to the 16th–19th centuries. Undisturbed 16th–18th century cultural layers were recorded at a depth of up to 3.2–4.03 m. In test pit 4, part of a wooden construction made of boards and several small timbers was found. In test pit 5 the arched foundations of a building from the second half of the 18th century were unearthed.

lt: 2006 m. LP vykdë archeologinius žvalgymus Vilniaus senojo miesto vietoje, pastato Žygimantų g. 3 vidiniame kieme, Žygimantų g., T. Vrublevskio g. ir Karaliaus Mindaugo paminklo zonoje. Žvalgymai susiję su elektros kabelių tranšėjos kasimu [p. 387].
en: In 2006 the LP conducted a survey in Vilnius Old Town in the courtyard of the building at Žygimantų St. 3, on Žygimantų and T. Vrublevskio Sts., and in the area of the monument to King Mindaugas in connection with the excavation of an electric cable trench. A 278 m long route was surveyed (a total area of 164.02 m²). A mixed cultural layer, through which utility lines had already been laid, was discovered. 17th–20th century finds were found: pottery sherds, stove, roof, and floor tile fragments, metal and glass artefacts, and 19th–20th century coins.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai Pylimo g. 47 / Gėlių g. 2
lt: 2006 m. Vilniuje, Pylimo g. 47 / Gėlių g. 2 esančio pastato rūsiuose ištirti 6, o pastato patalpose (planuojamų iškasti rūsių vietose) – 4 šurfai. Visi šurfai buvo 4 m² ploto (iš viso ištirtas 40 m² plotas). Šurfai kraštinėmis derinti prie pastato sienų ir išplanuoti patalpų kampuose [p. 388].
en: In 2006, 6 test pits were excavated in the basements of the building located at Pylimo St. 47 / Gėlių St. 2 in Vilnius and 4 test pits in the building’s rooms. In all an area of 40 m² was excavated. The construction of the basements dates to the early 18th – 1st half of the 19th century. Finds from no earlier than the 18th century and chance pottery sherds from probably the 16th–17th century were found in the layers excavated in them. Excavations were conducted in two of the building’s rooms. They were built in the early 18th – 1st half of the 19th century. An earlier stone pavement and brick wall fragments were discovered in the rooms. A cultural layer with finds dating to the 17th–18th centuries (stove tile fragments, pottery sherds, and animal bones) was recorded in them.

t: Tyrinėjimai Gedimino prospekte ties Lukiškių aikšte
au: Zabiela, Gintautas; Ramanauskienė, Justina; Suncovas, Vaidotas
lt: 2006 m. vykdyti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, rekonstruojamoje Gedimino pr. dalyje tarp Vasario 16-osios ir V. Kudirkos g., šalia Lukiškių aikštės. Tai mažiausiai užstatyta prospekto dalis. Jos P pusėje dabar stovi du XIX a. pabaigoje statyti pastatai: 1897–1899 m. – teismo rūmai (Gedimino pr. 40) ir 1900–1902 m. – mergaičių gimnazija (Gedimino pr. 42; dabar – Lietuvos muzikos akademijos centriniai rūmai). Prospekto Š pusėje yra XVIII a. pradėta formuoti Lukiškių aikštė [p. 390].
en: In 2006 an excavation was conducted in Vilnius next to Lukiškės Square in the part of Gedimino Avenue being reconstructed between Vasario 16-osios and V. Kudirkos Sts. On the S side of the avenue stand two brick public buildings that were built in the late 19th – early 20th century while on the N side is Lukiškės Square which began to form in the 18th century and was used as a market place until the mid-20th century. A 3000 m2 area was excavated in the avenue’s roadway and another 4000 m2 under the pavements but no undisturbed cultural layer was found. The chance finds collected such as a glass bottle bottom with an inscription are connected to the market place activities and date to the 19th – early 20th century.

lt: 2006 m. Vilniuje, Aguonų g. 17 vykdyti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai. Iki 1940 m. šioje teritorijoje veikė tabako fabrikas. Fabriko pastatai sukoncentruoti sklypo R dalyje, prie Aguonų g. Čia buvo pastatytos dirbtuvės, žaliavų sandėliai, ekonominė parduotuvė, administracinis pastatas su valdininkų butais, svečių kambariais, darbininkų patalpomis, kanceliarija, arklidės ir t. t. Sklypo V dalyje (prie Mindaugo g.) esantys mūriniai gamybinės paskirties statiniai statyti po 1940 m. Žvalgomųjų tyrinėjimų metu iškasti 7 šurfai, iš viso ištirtas 22,45 m2 plotas. Fiksuotas 2–3,7 m storio kultūrinis sluoksnis. Iki 1–1,45 m gylio fiksuoti XX a. datuotini permaišyti kultūrinio sluoksnio horizontai [p. 393].
en: 7 test pits were excavated during an evaluation conducted in Vilnius at Aguonų St. 17. In all an area of 22.45 m2 was excavated. A 2–3.7 m thick cultural layer was recorded during the evaluation. Jumbled cultural layer horizons that date to the 20th century were recorded at a depth of 1–1.45 m. Iron shoe heel plates, wrought nails, household pottery sherds, and fragments of flat stove tiles were discovered in deeper layers. The finds date to the 16th–19th centuries. Fragments of stone pavement and a building dating to the late 19th – first half of the 20th century were also found.

lt: 2006 m. Bokšto g. 21A vykdyti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai, kurių metu iškasti penki 2 x 2 m dydžio šurfai (iš viso ištirtas 20 m2 plotas). Remiantis istoriniais duomenimis, tirtame sklype XVIII a. pradėti statyti mūriniai pastatai. Klasicizmo laikotarpiu galutinai susiformavo sklypo užstatymas, aptvertas mūrine tvora. Tačiau tyrinėjimų metu neaptikta jokių užstatymo pėdsakų. Fiksuotas 1,5–3,3 m storio kultūrinis sluoksnis. Apatinis jo horizontas datuojamas XVII a [p. 395].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted at Bokšto St. 21A, during which 5 test pits were excavated (an excavated area of 20 m2). During the evaluation a 1.5–3.3 m thick cultural layer was recorded. 17th–20th century finds (an iron key, household ceramics, flat stove tile fragments, and part of a pipe) were discovered. The bottom horizons of the cultural layer date to the 17th century. No traces of structures were found during the evaluation.

t: Žvalgymai L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus g. / Universiteto g
lt: 2006 m. vykdyti archeologiniai žvalgymai Vilniuje, L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus g. / Universiteto g. Žvalgymai vykdyti renovuojant šiluminę trasą ir tiesiant naują jos atšaką (Universiteto g.). Atkarpoje A darbai pradėti L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus g. R dalyje. Atkarpos ilgis – 85 m. Atkastas ir dalinai demontuotas betoninis šiluminës trasos kolektorius. Kastos 1,5–2 m pločio, 1,3 m gylio tranšėjos. Nesuardytas kultūrinis sluoksnis nepasiektas – žvalgymų metu fiksuotas pilkos maišytos žemės sluoksnis su gausiomis griuvenomis, skalda, XX a. buitinėmis ir statybinėmis šiukšlėmis [p. 397].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in Vilnius on L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus St. / Universiteto St. The evaluation was made in a trench up to 3 m wide that was excavated to a depth of up to 1.3 m. No undisturbed cultural layer horizons were reached. During the evaluation 4 brick wall fragments, a stone pavement fragment, fragments of Vilnius’ 16th century defensive wall, and fragments of a 19th century brick sewer were discovered and recorded. Chance 17th–19th century finds were collected during the evaluation.

lt: 2006 m. buvo tęsiami 1995 m. pradėti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniaus reprezentacinių rūmų ansamblio teritorijoje (S. Daukanto a. 3, Universiteto g. 6 ir Totorių g. 28) [p. 398].
en: In 2006 investigations were conducted on the grounds of the Vilnius Representative Hall complex at S. Daukanto Square 3, Universiteto St. 6, and Totorių St. 28. An excavation was conducted inside building 03A (formerly a coach house in the early 19th century) (an excavated area of 227.6 m2) as well as outside the building (an excavated area of 172 m2). 3 test pits (with an excavated area of 32.3 m2) were dug on the grounds of the park. A field survey (with a surveyed area of about 116 m2) was made near the N fence surrounding the park (Liejyklos St.). During the excavation, fragments of wooden constructions dating to the 16th–18th centuries and of Vilnius’ 16th century defensive wall were discovered as well as finds dating to the 16th–20th centuries.

lt: 2006 m. pratęsus senamiesčio P apvažiavimo statybos darbus (atkarpoje tarp Aušros Vartų ir Vanagėlio g.), kartu vykdyti ir archeologiniai žvalgymai. Žvalgytas 7970 m² plotas [p. 402].
en: In 2006 a survey was conducted at the construction site of the Vilnius S bypass (the segment between Aušros Vartų and Vanagėlio Sts.). During them, a group burial (with five individuals) that dates to the early 19th century was discovered at the entrance to Lapų St. It is possible to connect this grave site with the retreat of Napoleon’s army from Moscow in the winter of 1812–1813. Two storage pits dating to the 16th–17th century were found beside the grave. In reshaping the hill located to the W of Lapų Street, a fragment of a brick building dating to the late 19th – first half of the 20th century was discovered on the S slope. An oven dating to the late 19th – first half of the 20th century and fragments of a brick building dating to the mid-18th – early 20th century were discovered in the segment near the intersection of Aušros Vartų and Geležinkelio Sts.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai ir žvalgymai Šv. Stepono g. 29
lt: 2005–2006 m. vykdyti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai ir archeologiniai žvalgymai Vilniuje, Šv. Stepono g. 29. Sklype numatytos statybos – buvusio užstatymo atkūrimas. Planuojama statyti gyvenamąjį namą su komercinės paskirties patalpomis. Nagrinėjamas sklypas yra Vilniaus senamiesčio 84 kvartalo teritorijoje [p. 404-405].
en: In 2005–2006 a field evaluation and field survey were made in Vilnius at Šv. Stepono St. 29. The evaluation was conducted first. 4 test pits were excavated (an excavated area of 17 m2). In them were discovered the remains of a brick structure dating to the late 19th – 1st half of the 20th century: the remains of basements filled with rubble and fragments of ground floor floors and walls. No finds of archaeological value were discovered. The cultural layer’s early horizons were probably destroyed during construction work in the 19th – 20th century. Because no cultural layer was found, the investigation was thereafter restricted to a field survey (an area of 1829 m2 was surveyed). No cultural layer or valuable finds were discovered during it.

lt: 2006 m. vykdyti archeologiniai žvalgymai Vilniuje, Žemaitijos g. 13/10, naujo gyvenamojo namo ,,Mikalojaus žiedas“ statybos vietoje. Naujasis pastatas iškils vietoj nugriauto PRI pastato (statyto XX a. 7–8 dešimtmečiais). Archeologinių žvalgymų tikslas – nustatyti, ar griaunamo pastato vietoje dar yra išlikusių nesuardyto kultūrinio sluoksnio horizontų. Žvalgyta statybinio laužo ir grunto išvežimo darbų metu [p. 407].
en: In 2006 an evaluation was conducted in Vilnius at Žemaitijos St. 13/10, the construction site for a residential home. The construction of the future flats began in place of the demolished PRI building, which had been built in place of buildings demolished in 1944 (that had been built and reconstructed in the 19th – early 20th century). A 4 x 6 m area with an undisturbed cultural layer that was 1.9–2.7 m thick was discovered in the S part of the small inner courtyard. Its top horizons date to the 18th–19th century while 16th–17th century finds were discovered in the bottom horizons. In excavating the trench in the inner courtyard at Šiaulių St. 8, fragments of two parallel foundations were found. These are probably the remains of a former mid-19th century building with a basement. On the W edge of Šiaulių St. were discovered the remains of an old structure (pre-1944): the foundation of an exterior basement wall of a building (with bay windows) that stood near the street and fragments of the demolished interior walls. The remains of earlier (18th–19th century) structures were discovered near Žemaitijos St. (on the NW corner of the lot) and near the NW corner of the building at Šiauli

t: Žvalgymai Dzūkų ir Vilniaus gatvėse Valkininkuose
lt: 2006 m. lapkričio mėnesį LII MTS vykdė archeologinius žvalgymus Valkininkų miestelio (Varėnos r.) centrinėje dalyje, Dzūkų ir Vilniaus g. Archeologinių žvalgymų metu planuojamoje šviesolaidžio kabelio trasos vietoje stebėti žemės kasimo darbai 390 m ilgio ruože, iki 40 cm pločio ir nuo 70 iki 120 cm gylio tranšėjose. Stebėtos teritorijos bendras plotas siekė iki 156 m2 [p. 412].
en: In 2006 the LII MTS conducted evaluations in a section of cable trench, 390 m long, up to 0.4 m wide, and 0.7–1.2 m deep, on Dzūkų and Vilniaus Sts. in Valkininkai (Varėna Dist.). A total area of 156 m2 was evaluated. Up to the projected depth of 0.7 m, the horizons dated to the 19th–20th centuries. During the evaluation 16 artefacts were discovered, such as household pottery sherds, coins, and other metal artefacts. Some of the finds (a Sigismund III coin dating to 1st half of the 17th century) also indicate that the horizons could contain artefacts older than the 19th–20th centuries.

lt: 2006 m. rudenį vykdyti Vilniaus P aplinkkelio 7,6–27,24 km tarp A1 Vilniaus–Kauno–Klaipėdos ir A3 Vilniaus–Minsko kelių (Vilniaus r.) žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai. Aplinkkelis suprojektuotas apeinant Rudaminos gyvenvietę. Kelio trasa prasideda į ŠR nuo Baltosios Vokės gyvenvietės, toliau ji eina į ŠV nuo Pagirių, Valčiūnų gyvenvietės ŠV pakraščiu, Dusinėnų kaimo laukais ir mišku. Už Vilniaus–Lydos kelio aplinkkelis suprojektuotas Pyšnos kaimu bei mišku, toliau Petešos kaimo Š pakraščiu, Pakalnių, Totoriškės, Šveicarų kaimų laukais bei miškais. Aplinkkelis baigiasi už Gegužinės miško, Vilniaus–Minsko kelio 16,05 km. Archeologinių žvalgomųjų tyrimų tikslas – patikrinti, ar suprojektuotoje trasoje yra archeologinių objektų. Tyrinėjimų metu ištirta 40 šurfų. Iš viso ištirtas 40,90 m2 dydžio plotas. Nustatyta dvylika vietų, kuriose prieš tiesiant kelią reikės atlikti archeologinius tyrinėjimus [p. 471].
en: In 2006 a field evaluation was conducted in the 7.6–27.24 km segment of the Vilnius S bypass (Vilnius Dist.). The evaluation’s aim was to check whether there are any archaeological objects in the planned route. 40 test pits with a total area of 40.90 m2 were excavated during the evaluation. Hand built, partially thrown, and thrown pottery, the bridle bit and many flint finds were discovered in the test pits and in their vicinity. The discovered pottery dates from the 1st millennium to the 19th century. The flint finds found in various locations of the planned bypass have been preliminarily dated from the Palaeolithic to the early Bronze Age. During the evaluation, 12 sites were established, at which excavations need to be made prior to the construction of the road.

t: Žvalgymai ir žvalgomieji tyrimai Pietų ir Rytų Lietuvoje
lt: 2006 ir ankstesniais metais autorius savo iniciatyva vykdė archeologinius žvalgymus ir žvalgomuosius tyrimus Rytų ir Pietų Lietuvoje. Šių tyrimų metu pakoreguotos kelių objektų teritorijos bei aptikta daug naujų archeologijos vertybių, kurių nemaža dalis yra unikalūs mūsų krašto praeities paminklai. Taip pat 2006 m. buvo atlikti 3 privačių žemės sklypų žvalgomieji tyrimai Kirdeikiškės, Pašvenčio (Švenčionių r.) ir Pasienių (Vilniaus r.) kaimuose, kur tyrimų metu taip pat aptikta vertingų archeologinių objektų. Daugelis šių naujai surastų archeologijos vertybių aptikta ir jų teritorijos nustatytos taikant kuo mažesnius destrukcinius archeologinius tyrimus bei pasitelkiant gretutinių mokslų (paleogeografijos, geomorfologijos, botanikos, dirvožemio tyrimų) teikiamus duomenis [p. 473].
en: In 2006 and earlier years the author has conducted field surveys and evaluations in East and South Lithuania. During these investigations, the territory of the settlement at the foot of Akvieriškė hill fort (Švenčionys Dist.) was significantly corrected by expanding it to the N and 9 new archaeological sites were discovered: 7 ancient settlement, 1 former village site with the remains of an earlier ancient settlement site, and 1 hill fort. The following ancient settlement were identified: Lapainia 2 (Kaišiadorys Dist.), which dates to the Final Palaeolithic – Mesolithic period, Papiškės and Pasieniai (both in Vilnius Dist.), which date to the Stone and Iron Ages, Pervieniškės (Žemaitiškė) 6, which dates to the Middle Neolithic, and Kirdeikiškė (both in Švenčionys Dist.), which dates to the Final Palaeolithic – early Neolithic. Dabinta village site (Kaišiadorys Dist.) is on the second terrace above the floodplain on the bank of the Nemunas. Sherds of thrown – partially thrown vessels and osteological finds were discovered in especially large quantities during the survey and the remains of destroyed stoves were located. The discovered finds date to the 15th–19th centuries. Finds from

lt: 2005 m. lapkričio mėnesį apie 150 x 250 m lauko plote, kurį riboja Musės upė (iš Š ir ŠV), kelias Vilnius–Širvintos (iš ŠR), pilkapyno miškas (iš PR) ir magistralinio dujotiekio trasa (iš P), buvo pastebėta keramikos trupinių, rastas siauraašmenis kirvis numušta pentimi. Planuojant žvalgomuosius tyrimus manyta, jog lauke gali būti sunaikintų pilkapių liekanų arba XIV a. pabaigos – XV a. kapų [p. 488].
en: In 2006 a field evaluation (7 test pits with a total area of 10 m2) was conducted at the Turlojiškės find spot (Širvintos Dist.). Found: hand built pottery sherds with smooth and rough surfaces from a 2nd–3rd century settlement (dated on the basis of a Antoninus Pius bronze dupondius minted in 153–154; in a private collection); a narrow-bladed axe and ornament fragment from destroyed barrows from the 2nd half of the 1st millennium; a 15th century earring, which together with the late 14th–15th century cast ring brooch previously found here (in a private collection) could have come from destroyed burials from this period. The 17th–19th century thrown pottery, a roof tile fragment, nails, and coins (in private collections) should be connected with a homestead (?) located here in the 17th–18th century.

lt: 2006 m. LII MTS vykdė archeologinius žvalgymus Vilniuje, Gedimino pr. 22, susijusius su pastato rekonstrukcijos darbais [p. 428].
en: In 2006 field survey was performed in Vilnius at Gedimino Ave. 22. An area 160 m2 in size was surveyed. Disturbed 2–3.4 m thick cultural layers were recorded in the greater part of the area. The remains of a limekiln dating to the 16th century were discovered and partially exposed in the S part of the courtyard. The remains of 18th–19th century brick structures were also recorded.

lt: 2006 m. Vilniuje, Kalvarijų g. 2 numatomose komunikacijų tiesimo vietose atlikti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai, kurių metu kiemo V bei P dalyje iškasti septyni šurfai. Bendras tirtas plotas – 38,75 m2. Mechanizuotu būdu tiesiant komunikacijas, šiame objekte taip pat atlikti archeologiniai žvalgymai, žvalgytas 43,2 m2 dydžio plotas [p. 436].
en: In 2006 field evaluation (38.75 m2 were excavated) and field survey (43.2 m2 were surveyed) were conducted in Vilnius at Kalvarijų St. 2. The earliest cultural layers in test pits 1 and 2 reach the turn of the 19th century. The remains of the foundation from a brick structure from that period were discovered at this location. In test pit 3 a disturbed burial from the second half of the 17th century was discovered. In test pit 7 the remains of a kiln were unearthed. The kiln was used in the late 17th – first half of the 18th century, probably during the construction of the Church of St. Raphael and the monastery. It was used to burn lime and fire construction pottery. In test pit 6 the contours of a burnt lime pit and the fragments of a structure’s foundation were recorded.

lt: 2006 m. buvo atliekami žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, buvusių Vingrių šaltinių versmių aplinkoje. Tyrinėjimai vyko teritorijoje, kurioje planuojami kvartalo rekonstrukcijos darbai [p. 438].
en: During field evaluation 10 test pits (with a total excavated area of 45.81 m2) were excavated in the vicinity of Vingriai springs in Vilnius. A 17th–20th century cultural layer was recorded and household pottery sherds, fragments of glass artefacts, the remains of metal artefacts, and coins were found. Fragments of wooden water pipes, through which water flowed from Vingriai springs, were discovered. Fragments of two brick structures probably connected with the exploitation of Vingriai springs were unearthed. The excavations provided information about the water pipe construction that occurred at this location.

lt: 2006 m. buvo tęsti vadinamosios F. Valickio vilos tyrimai, pradëti 2005 m. (ATL 2005 metais, Vilnius, 2006, p. 189–193). Dar 2005 m. nustatyta, kad visi namo pamatai mūryti vienu metu iš iki 25 cm skersmens riedulių apie 1 m gylio griovyje, kurio dugne – vidutinio stambumo žvyras. Tada pastato viduje aptikta arka buvo užpilta iki 2006 m. tyrinėjimų sezono [p. 442].
en: The excavation, which was begun in 2005, of the so-called villa of F. Valickis in Vilnius continued in 2006. Inside the building, the excavation of arches, which were part of a kiln, was completed. After excavating outside the villa, the remains of arches from another two kilns were discovered in a small area.

t: Preliminarūs 2006 m. archeologinių kasinėjimų zooarcheologinės medžiagos tyrimų rezultatai
au: Daugnora, Linas; Daugnorienė, Vida; Suncovas, Vaidotas
en: Bones found at various archaeological sites and dating to different periods were studied in 2006 at the Osteological Laboratory of the LVA Department of Anatomy and Physiology. The osteological material excavated during archaeological expeditions is kept in the Laboratory’s storage facilities.

t: Preliminarūs 2006 m. archeologinių kasinėjimų antropologinės medžiagos tyrimų rezultatai
au: Jankauskas, Rimantas; Barkus, Arūnas; Urbanavičius, Agnius
lt: Po 2006 m. archeologinių tyrinėjimų sezono VU MF ištirti apie 878 asmenų palaikai iš griautinių (846 asmenų palaikai) ir degintinių (32 asmenų palaikai) palaidojimų (iš viso iš 34 paminklų). Buvo tiriamos taip pat ir ankstesnių sezonų metu rastos ir dėl įvairių priežasčių tik dabar gautos kremacijos; jas tiriant dalyvavo archeologas L. Kurila. Medžiaga išvalyta, konservuota, identifikuota ir dokumentuota. Mokslinės informacijos požiūriu vertinga medžiaga saugoma katedros saugyklose ir prieinama tolesniems detalesniems tyrimams [p. 509].
en: In all, the remains of about 878 individuals (846 inhumations, 32 cremations) from 34 sites were examined macroscopically and under low magnification. The materials were processed in accordance with the standard procedures (cleaning, preservation, identification, and documentation). Cremated bones from previous years, which had been previously been stored at other institutions, were likewise included in this analysis. Archaeologist L. Kurila also participated in the examination of the cremations. Non-human bones found in cremations were separated out and transferred to the LVA Osteological Laboratory for examination. Any scientifically valuable materials were stored in the depositories of VU MF and made available for further analysis. This paper presents a short report on these materials. The analysis of Iron Age cremations revealed that individuals of both sexes and of various ages, including children, were regularly cremated.Among the larger cemeteries from the 2nd millennium AD, burials from Dubingiai castle were further analysed (55 individuals, some of whom bore signs of healed traumas caused by edged weapons). The age profiles of the burials from Aguonų St. in Vilnius (149 in

lt: 2004 m. archeologiniai tyrinėjimai ir žvalgymai buvo vykdomi Bernotų (Vilniaus r.) piliakalnio su papėdės gyvenviete ir senkapio aplinkoje. Dar 2003 m. čia atlikti žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai, susiję su planuojamo privažiavimo prie geografinio Europos centro rekonstrukcija bei projektuojama automobilių stovėjimo aikštele (žr. ATL 2003 metais, V., 2005, p. 40-42) [p. 53].
en: In 2004 an area of 70 m2 was investigated at the S outskirts ofthe territory of the Bernotai hillfort (Vilnius district). A 1.8 m thick cultural layer was found. It consisted of the upper layer formed of brown sand sliding from the hill-fort slopes and the lower layer formed of black-earth and containing potshards datable to the 1st millennium A. D., ceramic spindles and knifes. The layer also contained flint finds datable to the Stone Age and Old Bronze Age.

lt: 2003 ir 2004 m. buvo pratęsti Staviškių pilkapyno (Vilniaus m.) tyrinėjimai. 1998, 1999 ir 2002 m. archeologinių tyrinėj imų metu surasti trys pilkapiai, du iš jų ištirti. Taip pat rastos II—IV a. gyvenvietės žalvario lydimo dirbtuvių liekanos (žr. ATL 1998 ir 1999 melais, V., 2000, p. 168-170; ATL 2002 metais, V., 2005, p. 62). Pilkapiai vizualiai iš aplinkos neišsiskiria. Jų sampilai sulyginti Neries potvynių metu. 2003 ir 2004 m. Staviškėse ištirtas 254,5 m2 plotas [p. 76].
en: In 2003-2004 in the Staviškės barrow cemetery (Vilnius City) the barrow No. 3 was excavated; 254.5 m2 in total. Tire barrow was 6-7 m in diameter; it had a ditch and a pit. Two cremations were found in the ditch and the pit. The first cremation contained a small knife, tiny fragments of a bronze strap and a potsherd. The second cremation contained an awl. There were more loose finds in the ditch: a bracelet fragment and an awl. Most probably, they came form the third burial. At the bottom of the pit there were a bracelet, a bead and two spindles. They should be attributed to offerings. The barrow is datable to the 8th-10th century. Besides that, 8 test trenches were excavated. Two new barrow sites and one pit also attributable to a barrow were found.

lt: 2002 m. atnaujinti Gudelių (Lenkiškių) pilkapyno (Vilniaus r.) (A 1237P) tyrinėjimai (žr. ATL 2002 melais, V., 2005, p. 69-72; ATL 2003 metais, V., 2005, p. 91-93) buvo tęsiami 2004 m. Pilkapyno teritoriją kertančioje aukštos įtampos elektros linijos proskynoje po 1987-1989 m. bei 2002 ir 2003 m. vykdytų tyrinėjimų liko trijų buldozeriu nustumdytų pilkapių liekanos ir šeši suplokštėję pilkapiai. 2004 m. ištirtas pilkapis 9(56), buvęs elektros linijos proskynoje, bei dvi perkasos 2003 m. buldozeriu pažeistoje paminklo teritorijos dalyje. Iš viso ištirtas 171,25 m2 plotas (121,25 m2 - pilkapio teritorijoje). Tyrinėjimai vykdyti pagal KVAD žalojamų archeologijos vertybių tyrimų programą [p. 80].
en: In 2004 in the Gudeliai (Lenkiškės) (Vilnius district) barrow cemetery the destroyed barrow No. 9(56) and two sites of 25 m2 each were investigated. The barrow was found to have a stone circle. No intact graves were found in the barrow, except of a few small cremated bones and two fragments of a clay spindle. The investigated barrow is typical to the East Lithuanian Barrow Culture and is dated to the middle or the 2nd half of the 1st millennium A. D. Excavations also revealed remains of earlier settlements. Artefacts typical to the Mesolithic and Iron Age were found. At both sites remains of a cultural layer belonging to a manor or a village datable from the 2nd half of the 17th century to the 18th (19th?) century, was discovered.

lt: 2004 m. VU tęsė Grabijolų (Žemaitiškių) pilkapyno II tyrinėjimus (žr. ATL 2001 metais, V., 2002, p. 92-93; ATL 2002 metais, V., 2005, p. 72; ATL 2003 metais, V., 2005, p. 94). Ištirtas vienas perartas miško priešgaisrinės juostos pilkapis 4(69) pilkapyno R pakraštyje (iš viso 100 m2), apaugusioje jaunomis pušaitėmis pievoje, po buvusio (sunykusio) dvaro langais [p. 83].
en: In 2004 in the eastern part of the Grabijolai (Žemaitiškės) (Vilnius district) barrow cemetery II one barrow No. 4(68) with a destroyed stone circle was excavated. Three cremation graves with iron, bronze and clay artefacts were found in the central part of the barrow. In the female grave No. 1 a clay spindle-whorl and a bronze spiral ring were found. In the central grave an iron shield boss, a battle-axe, a spearhead, a knife, a B-shaped buckle and a bronze spiral ring were found. In the male grave No. 3 only an iron spearhead was found. The investigated barrow is typical to the Eastern Lithuanian Barrow Culture and datable to the 6th century A. D.

lt: 2004 m. NM tęsė Sudotos pilkapyno I (Švenčioniųr., A 1118P) apardytų pilkapių tyrinėjimus. Apardytų Sudotos pilkapyno I pilkapių, esančių ant pirmos priešgaisrinės geležinkelio Vilnius-Turmantas linijos, tyrimai baigti 2002 m., 2003 m. ištirtas pažeistas ir apardytas pilkapis 54(6) (žr. ATL 1998 ir 1999 metais, V., 2000, p. 197-199; ATL 2000 metais. V., 2002, p. 73-74; ATL 2001 metais, V.. 2002, p. 93; ATL 2002 metais, V., 2005, p. 73-74; ATL 2003 metais, V., 2005, p. 94-95). 2004 m. ištirtas vienas pilkapis 55(7) [p. 86-87].
en: In 2004 the NM continued investigation of damaged barrows in the Sudota I barrow cemetery, which was started in 1998. The investigated barrow No. 55(7) had 12-14 m in diameter, including ditches and pits. No burials or individual artefacts were found. The barrow is datable to the 8th-12th century.

lt: 2004 m. KM atliko projektuojamos miesto magistralinių inžinerinių tinklų trasos, einančios centrine kultūros (archeologijos) paminklo - Kretingos senkapių (IP-2463/A) - teritorijos dalimi, archeologinius tyrimus [p. 122].
en: In 2004 in the Kretinga cemetery the KM excavated an area of 86.3 m2, in which 4 graves were found. The earliest one (the grave No. 4) dates back to the second half of the 16th century. It contained 2 male and 2 female burials; bodies orientated SW. Among the burial items there were 3 metal crosses, 3 wheel-made pottery shards and 2 silver half-groats struck by Grand Duke of Lithuania Sigismund Augustus in Vilnius in 1556 and 1564. The grave No. 1 contained 8 skeletons, heads orientated SW, laid in three layers one above another. On the top layer there was only 1 skeleton, 4 skeletons were found in the middle layer, and 2 on the bottom layer; between them there were fragments of one more skeleton: several ribs, humerus and hand-bones. Presumably the man tom to peaces by an explosion or by beasts and his remains were buried in a collective grave. Sculls of some skeletons were deformed: broken in the zone of temple, cheek or ear. Such deformations could be caused by incurred head hits. Specifics of the burials, military-type buttons found next to the skeletons and a round lead bullet imply that these were solders killed in Kretinga village during the Northern War in the first quarter

t: Vilniaus Žemutinės pilies valdovų rūmų vakarinis korpusas
lt: Atkuriant Valdovų rūmus 2004 m. buvo tęsiami jų V korpuso ir jo prieigų tyrimai. Nors išlikę V korpuso rūsiai buvo tirti dar 1994-1995 m., pradėjus statybos darbus tyrimai buvo pratęsti. Didesnės ar mažesnės apimties tyrimai vyko apie 2000 m2 plote, jų metu rasta apie 2600 radinių, tarp jų apie 50 monetų bei plombų [p. 133].
en: In 2004 investigations of the Western Block of the Sovereigns’ Palace and its vicinity was continued. The cellars themselves were investigated in 1994-1995; nevertheless many sites required further investigation. They covered an area of about 2000 m2. During the investigation about 2600 finds were collected, among them about 50 coins and seal tags. The cellars I and H were investigated, research of the cellars X and S was finished, and the top of the long cellar vault (Y) was excavated. The cellars were built in different periods varying from the late 15th to the early 17th century.

In 2004 in the old town of Vilnius at the site at the Bokšto Str. 17 an archaeological survey was performed. The survey covered the area of the planned earthworks and aimed to establish thickness, composition and dating of the cultural layer. Three test pits covering the total area of 12 m2 were investigated. Fragments of the cultural layer, separate potshards and a copper shilling coined by King John Casimir were found. On the basis of the potshards and numismatic materials the cultural layer was dated to the second half of the 17th - the second half of the 20th century. At the Bokšto Str. 21A another survey of the area of the planned earthworks was performed. It aimed to establish thickness, composition and dating of the cultural layer. Three test pits covering the total area of 12 m2 were investigated. In the test pits No. 1 and 2 (the southern part of the plot) no valuable cultural layer was found; piled layers dominated. In the test pit No. 3 (the northern part of the plot) alongside with loose crums of red bricks various ceramic shards (potshards and shards of stove-tiles) datable to the late 16th-18th centuiy were found.

lt: Vilniaus senamiestyje (A 1610K1), Šiltadaržio g. 4, buvo vykdomi archeologiniai tyrinėjimai. Jie vykdyti pastato viduje, jo centrinėje ir V dalyje, užsakovui norint atlikti pamatų tvirtinimo darbus, o vėliau planuojant įrengti rūsį [p. 215].
en: In the old town of Vilnius (A 1610K1) at the Šiltadaržio Str. 4 archaeological investigations were performed. They were executed inside the building in its central and western parts. An area of 45 m2 was investigated. During the investigation it was established that the cultural layer was up to 83 cm thick. 3 to 5 horizons of the cultural layer were investigated; the sterile soil was reached at the depth of Hafe 94.62 m. 164 artefacts and 93 bones were collected. Household pottery and constructional ceramics comprised the major share of the finds. Besides that, an iron knife with a riveted handle, forged nails and a glass cup foot fragment were found. According to the household pottery and constructional ceramics found during the investigation the cultural layer would be datable to the 17th - early 19th century. Fragments of the brick wall found during the investigation would be datable to the 18th-19th century.

lt: 2004 m. ištirtas 250 m2 plotas. Fiksuotas iki 2,8 m storio XVI a. pradžios - XX a. kultūrinis sluoksnis. Išskirti 9 pagrindiniai kultūrinio sluoksnio horizontai. Viršutinis iki 1,4 m storio siekiantis horizontas yra pats vėlyviausias, datuojamas XIX a. pabaiga - XX a. Į sąrašą įtraukti 1065 radiniai [p. 216].
en: In 2004 the archaeological investigations at the Užupio Str. 10 / Malūnų Str. 2 in Vilnius (A 1610K1) were continued. This was the third season of investigations performed at the site. An area of 250 m2 was investigated. The early 16th-20th century cultural layer up to 2.8 m thick was established. 9 major horizons of the cultural layer were investigated. Materials of the mid 16th-17th century prevailed. Household pottery and constructional ceramics comprised the major share. We should admit a unique tile (or stove-tile) fragment (it has no analogue in Lithuania). Among the individual finds bone processing waste should be mentioned. During the investigations of 2004 brick and wooden constructions were discovered at the site. Remains of the brick buildings are datable to the early or mid 17th century and the mid 18th-19th century. Remains of the wooden structures included two cribs of wells and an unidentified construction made of planks and logs. The wooden structures are datable to the early or mid 17th century. The primary purpose of the wells and wooden structures remains unclear; nevertheless their proximity and stratigraphic identity with the well No. 2 imply that they comprise

lt: 2004 m. atlikti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai pastato Pylimo g. 41, Vilniuje, vidiniame kieme. Ieškota buvusio užstatymo pėdsakų, siekta nustatyti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir pobūdį [p. 218].
en: In July 2004 archaeological investigations were performed in Vilnius at the Pylimo Street 41; the cultural layer datable to the 17th-20th century was found. During the investigations a stone pavement fragment and a wooden construction foundation fragment datable to the first half of the 20th century were discovered. The earliest horizon of the cultural layer dated to the 17th century.

lt: 2004 m. 90 m2 plote atlikti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai ir apie 400 m2 plote žvalgymai pastato Pylimo g. 22, Vilniuje, patalpose ir aplinkoje [p. 219].
en: Archaeological investigations and surveys were performed at the Pylimo Str. 22, on the external side of the Vilnius Defensive Wall destroyed in the 19th century. Previously it used to be the Kačerga (Vingre) Rivulet bed drained in the 19th century. A brick manifold for the rivulet draining dating to the 19th century and remains of the adjacent underground structures were discovered. A wooden water-pipe fragment dating to the 19th century was found as well. The earliest archaeological finds collected at the investigated site dated to the 16th century.

lt: 2004 m. atlikti archeologiniai žvalgymai sklype Vilniuje, Universiteto g. 9 ir jo aplinkoje. Kasta iškasa transformatorinei, atlikti žvalgymai inžinerinių tinklų įrengimo vietoje [p. 223].
en: The archaeological survey performed in the old town of Vilnius at the Universiteto Str. 9 hardly provided any new data. Buildings of the site have been owned by the Vilnius University since 1572. In the inner yard of the building an underground sewage manifold was discovered. It dated to the late 19th - the first half of the 20th century. Structural remains of wooden constructions of the 16th century and some archaeological artefacts of the 16th-20th century were found as well.

lt: 2004 m. maždaug 800 m2 plote atlikti archeologiniai žvalgymai pastato Vilniuje, Žygimantų g. 2, S korpuso rūsiuose, korpuso aplinkoje bei vidiniame pastato kieme. Buvo tęsiami pastato remonto ir statybiniai darbai [p. 223].
en: An archaeological survey was performed at the Žygimantų Str. 2 in Vilnius. Presumably this site is located in the vicinity of the 16th century palace of the noble family Radvilas cleared down on the edge of the 18th / 19th century. Remains of brick structures datable to the 16th-17th century and attributable to the Radvilas Palace complex were found. The earliest finds discovered at the site dated to the 16th century.

lt: 2004 m. Vilniuje, Vilniaus g. 22 / Labdarių g. 1 esančiame kieme LP atliko archeologinius žvalgymus, susijusius su elektros kabelio tiesimo darbais. Tyrinėjama buvo Vilniaus senamiesčio kvartale 12 (buvusi posesija 716) [p. 225].
en: In 2004 in Vilnius in the yard of the building located at the Vilniaus Str. 22 / Labdarių Str. 1 an archaeological survey was performed. During that a 300 m long, 0.5 m wide and 0.7 m deep trench was excavated. The cultural layer found in the trench was disturbed during earlier earthworks. The northern profile of the trench sector No. 2 revealed a stone pavement fragment, whereas the eastern profile of the tench sector No. 3 revealed a corner of the 20th century building. The 17th-20th century finds were collected: fragments of pottery, flat and comice stove-tiles, buttons, coins, a bullet and a tag. The oldest find was a Polish temarium coined by Jogaila in 1393-1407.

lt: 2004 m. LII MTS vykdė didelės apimties archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniaus senojo miesto vietoje (A 1610K1), Vilniaus g. 31. Tyrinėjimus dviejų aukštų požeminės automobilių stovėjimo aikštelės vietoje užsakė AB „VITI“. Tyrinėjimų metu Vilniaus g. 31 pastato vidiniame kieme ištirtas 459 m2 plotas. Pastato P korpuse dvylikoje patalpų ištirtas bendras 355 m2 plotas. Iš viso Vilniaus g. 31 ištirtas 814 m2 bendras plotas [p. 226].
en: In autumn 2004 the LII MTS performed an extensive archaeological research at the Vilniaus Str. 31 (Vilnius city). In the yard and southern block an up to 1.80 m thick cultural layer datable to the 16th-20th century was established. There were loose finds of the 15th century were found, nevertheless the layer of that century failed to form. Fragments of 15 ovens dating to the 16th-17th century were discovered. Inside the southern block 3 levels of the former street pavements were found. The first level dated to the 17th-18th century; the second one to the 17th century and the third one to the 16th-17th century. The investigations revealed that in the 16th-18th century the street stretched 4-5 m northwards from the present Islandijos Street. In the southern block several fragments of the 16th-17th century buildings were discovered. People who lived in the buildings next to the street were involved in stovetile production and iron processing. At the premises adjacent to the present Islandijos Street in the sterile soil a ditch of an unidentified purpose was found. Stratigraphicly it could be dated to the 16th-17th century. During the investigations a unique artefact was found: a medal

lt: 2004 m. LP vykdė žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniuje, pastatų komplekso T. Kosciuškos g. 3, priklausančio LNM, trečiajame korpuse. Tyrinėjimai susiję su pastato remonto ir drenažo sistemos įrengimo darbais. Pastato rūsyje (cokoliniame aukšte) dviejose patalpose planuota apie 0,2 m pažeminti grindų lygį bei patalpų pasieniais iškasti griovius drenažo sistemai [p. 234].
en: In 2004 an area of 20 m2 was investigated in the cellar o f the third block of the building complex located at the T. Kosciuškos Str. 3 (Vilnius) called the Horains’ House. A fragment of floor paved with stones and a thin cultural layer of about 30 cm containing finds of the 17th (16th?)- 20th century were found. Artefacts collected during the survey comply with historical information saying that the building was built in the mid 18th century. Nevertheless some finds and remains o f earlier foundations imply that the site could have been inhabited already in the 16th-17th century.

lt: 2003 m. LII MTS ekspedicija atliko žvalgomuosius, o vėliau ir išsamius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Gedimino pr. namo 4 patalpose. Žvalgomųjų tyrinėjimų metu 170 m2 dydžio patalpoje ištirti 3 bendro 11 m2 ploto šurfai. Vėliau papildomai ištirtos 3 perkasos (154 m2). Iš viso ištirtas 165 m2 plotas [p. 237].
en: In 2003 the LII MTS expedition performed a survey and later a full-scale archaeological investigation inside the house at the Gedimino Av. 4. During the survey 3 test pits (11 m2 in total) were investigated in the premise of 170 m2. Later 3 more trenches covering the total area of 154 n r were excavated. The total area investigated covered 165 m2. A 1.1-1.6 m thick cultural layer datable to the mid 17th and the mid 19th-20th century were established. Three horizons of the cultural layer were investigated. 395 finds were collected. Most of them were shards of pottery and constructional ceramics datable to the first half of the 17th century, out of them fragments of stovetiles should be discussed exceptionally. Some of them were decorated with the coats of arms of Lithuanian and Polish nobles, one of them belonged to the Gusiewski family. Fragments ofthe armorial stove-tiles and stratigraphic data imply that before the war of 1655 during which Vilnius was occupied and burned by the troops of Muscovite Czar Alexiej Michailovich, the present site No. 4 hosted the Gąsiewski family palace. After the war and the plague the site was deserted. Its repopulation began only in the 19th century

lt: 2004 m. LII MTS ekspedicija atliko žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniuje, Aukštaičių g. sklype 2. Sklypas yra Vilniaus senamiesčio R dalyje, kairėje Vilnios pusėje, Aukštaičių g. S pusėje. Iš R pusės jis ribojasi su mūrine sklypo 4 tvora (gamyklos teritorija), iš S - su asfaltuota gatve. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą. Įvairiose vietose ištirti 6 bendro 24 m2 ploto šurfai, surasti 247 radiniai [p. 239].
en: The archaeological survey was performed by the LII MTS expedition. The survey aimed to establish thickness and chronology of the cultural layer and to identify locations of the buildings which used to be situated at the site of the future construction works. 6 test pits (24 m2 in total) were excavated and 247 finds were collected. Most of them (188 pieces) were pottery shards. Besides that there were 39 pieces of constructional ceramics, 9 metal items and 4 glass items. Most of the finds were refections of the 17th-18th century material culture, which was also proved by numismatic finds. During the excavations 5 coins were collected: two copper shillings of the John Casimir emission of 1661-1666 (one of them was false), one false Riga coin of Queen Christine of Sweden, one Russian denga of 1735 and one groat coined by August III in 1755.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai J. Basanavičiaus g. sklype 36
lt: 2004 m. LII MTS vykdė žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniuje, J. Basanavičiaus g. sklypo 36 (Valstybinė kelių direkcija) kieme, projektuojamo namo vietoje. Tyrimų tikslas - išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį, chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą. Tyrinėjamas sklypas yra už saugomos Vilniaus senamiesčio teritorijos ribų, todėl iki šiolei jis ir jo aplinka archeologiškai nežvalgyti [p. 240].
en: In 2004 the LII MTS expedition performed archaeological tests and later the survey in the territory stretching westwards from the protected Vilnius old town area. The surveying works were performed at the planned building construction site and in its vicinity. 5 test pits were excavated covering the total area of 37.76 m2. Besides that, the adjacent territory of 1330.5 m2 was surveyed. 25 finds were collected: potshards and fragments of constructional ceramics datable to the late 17th (?) - the second half of the 19th century.

lt: 2004 m. LII MTS ekspedicija atliko žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus, o vėliau ir archeologinius žvalgymus Vilniuje, Gedimino pr. 20, 22 bei 24 esančiuose kiemuose. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą projektuojamų statybų vietoje [p. 241].
en: In July-December 2004 the LII MTS expedition performed archaeological tests and later the survey of the yards located at the Gedimino Str. 20, 22 and 24 (Vilnius). The survey aimed to identify thickness and chronology of the cultural layer and the previous building patterns at the planned construction site. The cultural layer of the second half of the 16th-20th century was established at the site. In the plot No. 20 a hoard of coins and banknotes of the year 1919 was found. In the plot No. 22 remains of a brick building cellar dating to the late 16th - the first half of the 17th century, shards of pottery and constructional ceramics and remains of a leather belt with a gilded silver buckle and mountings datable to the late 16th century were found.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai A. Jakšto ir Kaštonų gatvių sankirtoje
lt: 2004 m. LII MTS ekspedicija vykdė žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus ir žvalgymus Vilniuje, sklype, esančiame Jakšto ir Kaštonų gatvių sankirtoje. Ši senamiesčio ir Lukiškių teritorijos dalis, esanti į V nuo Vilniaus g. bei į S nuo Gedimino pr., archeologiškai nežvalgyta [p. 243].
en: In 2004 the LII MTS expedition performed archaeological tests and surveys in the historical Lukiškės Suburb of Vilnius at the planned building construction site and in its vicinity. Testing the territory of 997 m2 6 test pits with the total area of 16 m2 were excavated, later the survey was performed. The investigation aimed to identify thickness and chronology of the cultural layer and the previous building patterns. At undisturbed locations a 0.5-1.2 m thick cultural layer dating to the 18th-20th century was established. In the southern part of the site remains of the 17th century wooden building were discovered, and layers of the road known from cartographic materials were investigated.

lt: LII MTS ekspedicija atliko žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniaus senamiesčio Š dalyje, dešinėje Neries pusėje - istoriniame Šnipiškių priemiestyje. Sklypas išsidėstęs kairėje, Kalvarijų g. V pusėje, teritorijoje, iš R pusės apribotoje Kalvarijų gatve. Iš P pusės sklypas siejasi su XVIII a. pradžioje statytos Šv. Rapolo bažnyčios ir greta esančio vienuolyno ansambliu. Tarp jo ir sklypo yra pėsčiųjų takas, orientuotas V kryptimi ir vedantis į dabartinę centrinę universalinę parduotuvę bei „Lietuvos“ viešbutį. Praeityje šis kelias vedė į Ukmergę. Iš Š ir ŠR pusės sklypas ribojasi su namais 4, 6; iš V pusės - su automobilių stovėjimo aikštele. Sklypas yra netaisyklingos formos - į ilgį nusidriekęs P-Š kryptimi. Žemės paviršius nedidelėje kiemo dalyje užžėlęs menka žole, o didesnėje dalyje padengtas asfaltu ir šaligatvio plytelėmis. Tyrinėjimai buvo atliekami sklypo kieme ir namo 2 patalpose. Siekia išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą. Iki šiol sklypas archeologiškai ir istoriškai tyrinėtas nebuvo [p. 244].
en: The survey research at the historical Šnipiškės Suburb of Vilnius was performed by the LII MTS expedition. During the survey 10 test pits covering 37.76 m2 in total were excavated, and 1207 finds were collected: fragments of the 17th-19th century pottery and constructional ceramics, bone, metallic and glass items. In various sectors of the site the cultural layer of different thickness and structure was established. Human burials of the 20th century, remains of the 17th century dwelling houses, and remains of the roaster of the late 17th century - year 1703 tobacco-pipes manufactory were discovered. Over 500 items and production glazing tools were found including matrixes, fragments of urchins as well as 132 pipes and their fragments (5 types could be distinguished).

lt: 2004 m. LII MTS ekspedicija vykdė žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrimus Vilniaus senamiesčio R dalyje - Užupio priemiestyje. Darbai vyko Malūnų g. sklypų 4, 6 kiemuose. Siekta išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą. Abejuose kiemuose ištirta po 6 bendro 51,17 m2 ploto šurfus, surasta 613 radinių [p. 246].
en: In 2004 the LII MTS expedition performed an archaeological survey research in the Užupis Suburb in the eastern part of the Vilnius old town. The survey pursued the goal to establish thickness and chronology of the cultural layer and the former building patterns. In each of the yards 6 test pits were excavated (51.17 m2 in total), and 613 finds were collected. In both plots the cultural layer which was from 1.4 m to 2.5 m thick and dated from the edge of the 16th / 17th century till the 20th century was established. Variations of the primary ground level implied that before this territory was urbanised, it was uneven and had height variations of 0.5 to 1.5 m. In the 17th and 18th centuries the ground was flattened and local draining works were performed. Stratigraphic data of the survey revealed that the primary building pattern of the site dated to the edge of the 16th / 17th century. Nevertheless the potshards found were datable to the late 14th - the first half of the 16th century and they implied that habitation the site started in that period. The layers of the 14th - the first half of the 16th century must have been destroyed during an intensive urbanisation of the 17th-18th c

lt: Žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus atliko LII MTS ekspedicija. Sklypas Totorių g. 20 yra Vilniaus senamiesčio 11 kvartale, teritorijoje į S nuo L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus g. sklypo 11. Tyrinėjimų vieta yra į R nuo Totorių g. namo 20 sienos, iš S besiribojanti su Totorių g. namo 18 ir Odminių g. namo 12 ugniasienės. Iš R pusės teritorija ribojasi su keliuku, vedančiu į L. Stuokos-Gucevičiaus g. kiemus 5, 9. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį ir chronologiją bei lokalizuoti buvusį užstatymą. Sklype buvo atidengti ir ištirti du bendro 10,8 m2 ploto (su tranšėja) žvalgomieji šurfai [p. 249].
en: The archaeological survey was performed by the LII MTS expedition. It aimed to identify thickness and chronology of the cultural layer and the previous building pattern. Two test pits with the total area 10.8 m2 (including the trench) were excavated at the plot. In undisturbed sectors a 1.8-1.9 m thick cultural layer dating to the late 16th / early 17th-20th century was established. 45 finds were collected in total: mostly fragments of pottery and constructional ceramics.

lt: 2004 m LII MTS vykdė žvalgomuosius archeologinius tyrinėjimus Vilniaus senamiesčio V dalyje, 8 kvartale, į V nuo buvusių Radvilų rūmų (dabar Nacionalinis dailės muziejus), Vilniaus ir Islandijos gatvių sankirtoje esančiame sklype. Darbai vyko kieme bei pastato viduje. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - išsiaiškinti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį, chronologiją bei buvusį užstatymą planuojamų statybų vietoje. Iš viso buvo ištirta 18 bendro 48,23 m2 ploto žvalgomųjų šurfų [p. 250].
en: In October 2004 the LII MTS expedition performed an archaeological survey in the western part of the old town of Vilnius westwards from the former Radvila family palace. 18 test pits were excavated covering 48.23 m2 in total. Stratigraphic data and random finds implied that in the yard and in the southern block of the building there was a cultural layer of the late 16th / early 17th-20th century. Pottery and constructional ceramics fragments were found; pottery fragments dominated. Constructional ceramics was represented by fragments of flat and vessel-shaped stovetiles datable to the 16th-18th century. A piece of stove-tile’s matrix was found as well.

t: Tyrinėjimai Ašmenos-Mėsinių-Dysnos g. sankirtoje (Vilniaus senojo miesto 60 kvartale)
lt: 2004 m. KPC archeologų grupė „Antiqua" pradėjo išsamius viso Vilniaus senojo miesto 60 kvartalo archeologinius tyrinėjimus, susijusius su kvartale buvusių namų atstatymo darbais [p. 251].
en: In 2004 a full-scale archaeological investigation of the block No. 60 of the old town of Vilnius located at the crossing of the Ašmenos, Mėsinių and Dysnos Streets was performed. The cultural layer of the 15th-19th century, traces of the 16th century water pipes, over 15 garbage pits of the 16th-19th century and a lot of artefacts of the 15th-20th century were found. Brick foundations of the 16th-19th centuries, stone pavements of different periods, cellars of the 16th-17th centuries and their fragments were discovered as well.

lt: 2004 m. atlikti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, Arklių g. 18, buvusio Bazilijonų vienuolyno teritorijoje, kur ištirtas 56,5 m 2 plotas, vienuolyno ūkinio kiemo V (pjūviai 1, 2), R (pjūviai 3, 5) ir Š (pjūvis 4) pusėse. Darbų tikslas buvo nustatyti kultūrinio sluoksnio storį, pobūdį ir ar šioje teritorijoje esama buvusių pastatų liekanų [p. 254].
en: In 2004 an archaeological survey research was performed in the territory of the fonner Basiliani Convent at the Arklių Str. 18 in Vilnius. An area of 56.5 m2 was investigated. It was established that the cultural layer was 1.7-2.9 m thick. The cultural layer horizon datable to the 17th century and archaeological artefacts of the 16th-19th century were found. Besides that, a fragment of the 17th century brick structure was discovered.

t: Žvalgomieji tyrinėjimai Gedimino pr. tarp Jogailos ir A. Jakšto g
lt: Vilniaus miesto savivaldybė toliau tęsė Gedimino prospekto Vilniaus mieste rekonstrukcijos darbus. 2004 m. buvo keičiamos dangos ir senos komunikacijos apie 220 m ilgio ir 20 m pločio atkarpoje tarp Jogailos ir A. Jakšto gatvių. Bendras keičiamų dangų plotas - per 4400 m2. Važiuojamosios gatvės dalies plotis šioje atkarpoje yra apie 10,5 m, šaligatviai - apie 5 m pločio. Darbų metu važiuojamoje kelio dalyje buvo iškastas lovys iki 110 cm gylio nuo šaligatvių viršaus (apie 2200 m2) ploto. Šaligatvių zonoje gruntas keistas iki 0,6 m gylio (apie 2200 m2 plote). Be to, žemiau projektinio lygio buvo keičiamos senosios komunikacijos, įrengta nauja lietaus nuotekynė. Šioje teritorijoje buvo atliekami žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai [p. 255].
en: The Vilnius City Municipality continued reconstruction of the Gedimino Avenue. In 2004 an archaeological survey covering about 2200 m2 was performed in the Gedimino Avenue section between the Jogailos and A. Jakšto Streets. It revealed that in most of the places both the primary surface and the cultural layer were destroyed. Nevertheless next to the corner of the Jogailos Str. an undisturbed cultural layer containing the 16th-17th century pottery, constructional ceramics and bones was found. There was a garbage pit with animal bones, shards of pots, plates and mugs, flat stove-tiles and glass. In front of the A. Vienuolio Str. a damaged roaster used for brick and tile production was discovered. Next to that there was a pit of production waste. During the investigations the roaster structure and its construction stages were established. Finds collected in its vicinity were preliminarily dated to the late 16th - early 17th century.

lt: 2004 m. Vilniuje, Bokšto g. 16 PR kiemo dalyje ištirtas vienas 5 m2 ploto šurfas, tyrinėta iki 2,42 m storio kultūrinio sluoksnio dalis [p. 261].
en: In 2004 one test pit with an area of 5 m2 was excavated at the south-eastern part of the yard at the Bokšto Str. 16 (Vilnius). At the depth of 1.52-1.69 m a fragment of the 17th century vaulted foundation built of yellow bricks was found. Down to the depth of 2.42 m the cultural layer of the 17th century was established. It contained pottery and constructional ceramics shards, glass, iron, lead and bronze items.

lt: 2004 m. pastato Bokšto g. 16 kiemo ŠV kampe iškastas 3,06 m2 ploto žvalgomasis šurfas, tyrinėta iki 1,6 m storio kultūrinio sluoksnio dalis [p. 262].
en: In 2004 in the north-western corner of the yard of the building at the Bokšto Str. 16 (Vilnius) one test pit with an area of 3.06 m2 was excavated. A 1.6 m thick fragment of the cultural layer was investigated. The cultural layer discovered dated to the 17th century. It contained a lot of finds: shards of the 17th century pottery and stove-tiles, silver and copper coins of the 17th century, a Dutch tobacco-pipe fragment, a lead tag, a mounting, a lead bullet and a belt buckle fragment. At the depth of 1.6 m there was the 17th century pavement with a duct. It was left undisturbed, because further archaeological investigations of the site are planned to be performed in the future.

lt: Pastatai Vilniuje, Didžiojoje g. 25 driekiasi R-V kryptimi nuo Didžiosios iki Stiklių g., formuodami du pereinamus kiemus - didesnį rytinį ir mažesnį vakarinį. 2004 m. Didžiojoje g. 25-14, 16 V kiemo ŠV korpuso pirmojo aukšto patalpose buvo atlikti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai numatomų įrengti rūsių vietose [p. 262].
en: In 2004 in two ground-floor premises of the building at the Didžioji Str. 25-14, 16 in Vilnius an area of 47 m2 was investigated, and a 2.6 m thick cultural layer datable to the first half of the 16th - early 18th century was discovered. At the depth of 0.3-0.7 m brick floor remains datable to the second half of the 17th - early 18th century were found. At the depth of 1.1-1.4 m there was a ground-level layer of the first half of the 17th century containing coins, pottery and stove-tile shards. At the depth of 1.8 a groundlevel layer datable to the second half of the 16th - early 17th century was reached; it contained finds of the respective period: pottery and stove-tile shards. Tweezers used in the production of lead bullets were found, too. Over this layer there was a pile of stove-tile shards typical to the second half of the 16th - early 17th century - destroyed stove remains. At the depth of 2.1 m a groundlevel layer of the middle and the second half of the 16th century was reached. It contained potshards and stove-tile fragments. The lowest stratigraphic layer reached at the depth of 2.4-2.45 m contained potshards datable to the first half of the 16th century.

In 2004 several archaeological surveys in the territory of the old town of Vilnius were performed. At the Savičiaus Str. 13 earthworks were perform ed rebuilding the former wall of the Augustinian Closter at the Savičiaus Str. The archaeological survey was performed at the site of the former wall. An area of 23 m2 was investigated, and a fragment of the cultural layer down to 1.1 m was investigated. Remains of the foundation the 17th century building preceding the church and relevant stone pavement fragments were discovered. The interior premises of the building had stone pavements. Width of the foundation implies that the building was low. It was destroyed in the 17th century, later its facade foundation or its fragments were used as a wall. The mixed earth layers contained finds of the standard 17th century pottery. In relation to the heating pipeline reconstruction in the inner yard of the building at the Vilniaus Str. 22, an area of 180 m2 was investigated and a 1.2 thick cultural layer fragment was surveyed. Most of the earthworks were performed at the locations of the old heating pipeline where no valuable cultural layers were found. In the locations of new trenches prior to

lt: 2004 m. Vilniuje, Subačiaus g. 83, buvusioje alaus daryklos teritorijoje, neužstatytoje sklypo dalyje buvo atlikti žvalgomieji archeologiniai tyrinėjimai, kurių metu ištirti 4 šurfai, iš viso 4 m2 plotas, aptiktas iki 1,71 m storio XIX a. pabaigos - XX a. kultūrinis sluoksnis. Šurfuose fiksuoti siuoksniai ir struktūros sietini su alaus daryklos funkcionavimo laikotarpiu XIX a. pabaigoje - XX a. pradžioje bei kita XX a. ūkine veikla [p. 266].
en: In Vilnius at the Subačiaus Str. 83, in the free sector of the former brewery site an archaeological survey was performed. During that 4 test pits with the total area of 4 m2 were excavated and an up to 1.71 m thick cultural layer datable to the late 19th-20th century was found. Remains of brick constructions and a wooden water manifold were discovered. Cultural layers and structurės found in the test pits were relevant to the brewery which functioned in the late 19th - early 20th century as well as to other economical activities of the 20th century. Individual finds collected dated to the 17th-19th century.

lt: 2004 m. buvo vykdomi archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, Šv. Pranciškaus ir Šv. Bernardino bažnyčios ir vienuolyno ansamblio teritorijoje, rekonstruojamo oficinos pastato (Maironio g. 10) vietoje. Avarinės būklės pastate, kurį numatyta pritaikyti vienuolyno reikmėms, atkasti ir tvirtinti pastato PV kampo pamatai, atlikta išorinių sienų pamatų hidroizoliacija, S pastato dalyje ir tarpuvartėje iškastos naujos rūsio patalpos, kurios sujungtos su jau esamu rūsiu. Ištirtas 349 m2 plotas [p. 267].
en: During the archaeological investigations of the site at the Maironio Str. 10 (the territory of the St. Francis and St. Bernard Church and Convent) an area of 349 m2 was investigated. Fragments of earlier brick structures (of the 16th-17th century) built prior to the officina were discovered. Besides that, fragments of the defensive walls of the city orientated W-E and SE were found. On the comer there was a defensive tower orientated NE-SW. Its purpose was to defend the eastern side of the former Bernadine’s Gates. Fragments of the western, eastern, northern and southern corners of the tower were excavated. The external dimensions of the rectangular tower were about 6.5 x 8.8 m. The foundation pits excavated in the churchyard territory contained a large number of human bones (not less than of 177 individuals) coming from destroyed graves of the 16th-17th century. The cultural layer was 1.6-4 m thick. It dated to the first half of the 16th-19th century. During the investigations 244 archaeological finds datable to the second half of the 16th-19th century were collected.

lt: 2004 m. buvo vykdomi archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, Šv. Mykolo g. 6 pastato P korpuso P patalpoje, kurioje numatyta įrengti rūsį [p. 269].
en: In 2004 archaeological investigations were performed at the Šv. Mykolo Str. 6 (Vilnius) in a newly-built cellar. During the investigations potshards and stove-tile fragments dating to the 15th-17th century were found. The cultural layer was up to 3 m thick.

lt: 2005 m. vykdyti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, pastato Pilies g. 42-1 patalpoje. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - ištirti kultūrinį sluoksnį naujai įrengiamo rūsio vietoje. Tirtas apie 20 m2 plotas [p. 270].
en: During the archaeological investigation performed in the premises located at the Pilies Str. 42-1 (Vilnius) an area of 21 m2 was investigated. The cultural layer was 3.8 m thick. The upper layer (going down to about 1-1.3 m) was dated to the 18th-19th century. The middle layer (in the depth from 1.3 m to 2 m) was dated to the second half of the 16th-17th century. The lowest layer contained no archaeological finds. Presumably it formed in the first half of the 16th century. Fragments of foundations datable to the second half of the 18th-19th century and earlier ones datable to the second half of the 16th-17th century were discovered.

lt: 2004 m. mėn. vykdyti archeologiniai tyrinėjimai Vilniuje, Žemaitijos g, 13/10, prie buvusio PRI pastato, pastatyto 1944 m. nugriautų pastatų vietoje. Tyrinėjimų tikslas - nustatyti ankstesnio užstatymo ribas Žemaitijos ir Šiaulių gatvėse. Tyrinėjimų metu buvo kasta 1 perkasa Žemaitijos g. ir 3 šurfai Šiaulių g. Bendras tirtas plotas - 81 m2 [p. 271].
en: In summer 2004 during the archaeological excavations performed at the corner of the Žemaitijos Str. and the Šiaulių Str. (Žemaitijos Str. 13/10) an area of about 81 m2 was investigated. During the investigation a fragment of the foundation of the external walls of the southern and eastern blocks of the preceding buildings (former possessions No. 330 and 331) were discovered. They attributed to four construction stages: the 18th century, the first half of the 19th century, the mid 19th century and the 20th century reconstruction. The cultural layer was about 2-3 m thick. The earliest cultural layer (of the 17th century) was destroyed during construction works performed in the 18th-20th century. Most of the Ends collected dated to 19th - the first half of the 20th century.

t: Žvalgomoji archeologinė ekspedicija Musės pakrantėse (Širvintų r.)
lt: Asmenine iniciatyva 2004 m. buvo žvalgoma Musės upės kairioji pakrantė 10 km ruože, abipus senojo ir naujojo kelio Vilnius-Panevėžys. Apie tirtą teritoriją surinkta daug duomenų iš istorinių dokumentų. Rezultatyvi buvo ir žvalgomoji archeologinė ekspedicija [p. 305].
en: In 2004 during the archaeological survey the expedition established several new archaeological and mythological sites: the Godiškiai Stone Age settlement (the 4th-6th millennium B. C.), the Godiškiai Iron Age settlement (the 1st millennium A. D.), the Godiškiai manor site (the 15th / 16th-20th century), the Kukovaitis Sacred Forest location (according to chronicler of the second half of the 15th century J. Dlugosz Grand Prince of Lithuania Algirdas was cremated in this forest in 1377), the Plikiškiai second barrow group and individual barrow and the Turlojiškiai barrow cemetery and supposed sanctuary.

t: Rytų Lietuvos ežerų povandeniniai archeologiniai žvalgymai
lt: 2004 m. ieškota naujų povandeninių archeologinių objektų Rytų Lietuvos ežeruose. Žvalgomojoje ekspedicijoje naudotasi surinkta informacija apie ežeruose minimus spėjamus archeologinius objektus ar pavienius radinius. Polinių gyvenviečių ieškota naudojantis ortofotografijomis, siekiant aptikti naujų šio tipo objektų, todėl parinkti geografine aplinka panašūs ežerai į Luokesų ežerą, kuriame buvo rastos polinės gyvenvietės. Žvalgytos ortofotografijose užfiksuotos ežerų seklumos [p. 316].
en: In 2004 archaeological underwater investigations were carried in five lakes of eastern Lithuania: the Širvys (Glitiškės) Lake (in Vilnius district); the Baltieji Lakajai Lake, the Perkalys Lake, the Rašia Lake (all in Molėtai district) and the Vilkokšnis Lake (in Trakai district). No particular archaeological finds was discovered.
